_comment: Each key is a finding the analyzer can emit. 'products' lists categories from products.json. Edit freely.

skin_texture.title: Smooth out skin texture
skin_texture.summary: The photo picks up some uneven texture on the cheeks or forehead. A simple, consistent routine usually shows results in 4–8 weeks.
steps: Cleanse gently twice a day — skip harsh scrubs, they can make texture worse.
Add a niacinamide serum (5–10%) once a day to refine pores and even texture.
Finish with a light moisturizer so skin stays smooth instead of tight.

skin_redness.title: Calm visible redness
skin_redness.summary: There's a bit more redness than average in the cheek area. Soothing ingredients and less irritation usually help.
steps: Use lukewarm water, not hot, when washing your face.
Look for calming ingredients like centella, azelaic acid or ceramides.
Wear sunscreen daily — UV makes redness more noticeable over time.
If redness is persistent or painful, a dermatologist is the best next step.

skin_tone.title: Even out skin tone
skin_tone.summary: Brightness varies a little between areas of your face (for example, forehead vs. cheeks). Sun protection is the single biggest lever here.
steps: Apply SPF 30+ every morning, even on cloudy days.
A vitamin C or niacinamide serum can gradually even out tone.
Be patient — tone changes take 6–12 weeks to show.

skin_oil.title: Control shine
skin_oil.summary: Some areas reflect a lot of light, which often reads as oily skin on camera.
steps: Use a gel cleanser in the evening to clear excess oil.
Try a BHA (salicylic acid) product 2–3 times a week.
Keep moisturizing with an oil-free formula — stripping skin can make it produce more oil.
Blotting papers are a quick fix before photos.

skin_undereye.title: Brighten the under-eye area
skin_undereye.summary: The under-eye area looks a bit darker than your cheeks. Sleep, hydration and a caffeine eye product can help.
steps: Aim for 7–9 hours of sleep and stay hydrated.
Use a caffeine eye serum in the morning to reduce puffiness.
Cold compresses for a few minutes help on rough mornings.

skin_maintain.title: Protect what's working
skin_maintain.summary: Your skin reads clear in this photo. A simple maintenance routine keeps it that way.
steps: Cleanse, moisturize, and use SPF every morning.
Drink water and keep a consistent sleep schedule.

beard_patchy.title: Shape or tidy facial hair
beard_patchy.summary: Facial hair looks uneven between the two sides of your face. Either a cleaner shape or a closer trim usually looks sharper.
steps: Pick one length and trim evenly — a short, even stubble often looks fuller than a patchy longer beard.
Define a neckline about two fingers above your Adam's apple.
Beard oil softens hair and makes coverage look more even.

beard_define.title: Sharpen your facial hair lines
beard_define.summary: Facial hair edges look soft in this photo. Crisp cheek and neck lines make a big difference in how groomed it looks.
steps: Use a trimmer with a detail head to clean up cheek and neck lines.
Trim every 3–5 days to keep edges sharp.

brows_tidy.title: Tidy your brows
brows_tidy.summary: Your brows differ a little between sides. Small brow grooming makes the face look more balanced and put-together.
steps: Brush brows upward with a clear brow gel.
Remove only stray hairs below the brow line and between the brows.
If unsure, a one-time professional shaping gives you a template to maintain.

lips_care.title: Keep lips smooth
lips_care.summary: A small, easy upgrade: hydrated lips look healthier in photos and in person.
steps: Use a lip balm with SPF during the day.
Apply a thicker balm before bed.

grooming_maintain.title: Keep up your grooming
grooming_maintain.summary: Grooming looks clean in this photo. A regular schedule keeps it consistent.
steps: Set a weekly reminder for trims and brow tidying.
Keep a lip balm and a small comb in your bag.

hair_frizz.title: Reduce frizz and flyaways
hair_frizz.summary: The hair outline shows a lot of fine flyaways. Moisture and a light styling product usually tame this.
steps: Use a conditioner every wash and a leave-in on damp hair.
Dry with a microfiber towel or T-shirt instead of a rough towel.
Finish with a small amount of light cream or oil on the ends.

hair_shape.title: Give your hair more structure
hair_shape.summary: Your hair could frame your face more. A cut with defined shape, styled with a light product, adds polish.
steps: Ask your barber or stylist for a cut that suits your face shape — show them a reference photo.
Use a matte clay or cream to add volume and texture.
Get trims every 4–6 weeks to keep the shape.

hair_not_visible.title: Retake with hair in frame
hair_not_visible.summary: Your hair was mostly out of frame or covered, so this score is a neutral estimate.
steps: Leave some space above your head when framing the shot.
Remove hats or hoods for a full read.

hair_maintain.title: Keep your hair in shape
hair_maintain.summary: Your hair looks neat in this photo. Regular trims keep the style sharp.
steps: Book trims every 4–8 weeks depending on length.
Use heat protectant if you style with heat.

symmetry_balance.title: Use grooming to boost balance
symmetry_balance.summary: Every face is a little asymmetric — that's normal. Grooming choices can make features look more balanced.
steps: Even out brow shape and thickness on both sides.
Try a slightly off-center part or textured style to soften asymmetry.
Shoot from straight on at eye level — tilted angles exaggerate differences.

pres_lighting.title: Find better light
pres_lighting.summary: Lighting in this photo is uneven or dim, which hides detail and can lower every score.
steps: Face a window during the day — soft natural light is the most flattering.
Avoid overhead lights only; they cast shadows under the eyes.
At night, a small LED or ring light in front of you works well.

pres_angle.title: Straighten the camera angle
pres_angle.summary: Your head is tilted or turned. A straight-on, eye-level angle reads more confident and gives a fairer analysis.
steps: Hold the camera at eye level, about an arm's length away.
Keep your chin level and your face toward the lens.

pres_expression.title: Relax into your expression
pres_expression.summary: A relaxed, approachable expression makes a big difference in how you come across.
steps: Try a slight, natural smile — think of something that genuinely makes you smile.
Relax your forehead and jaw; tension shows on camera.

pres_framing.title: Frame the shot better
pres_framing.summary: Your face is very small, very large or off-center in the frame.
steps: Fill about a third to half of the frame with your face.
Center your face and leave a little space above your head.

pres_blur.title: Keep the photo sharp
pres_blur.summary: The photo looks soft or blurry, which hides detail.
steps: Wipe your camera lens.
Hold still and tap to focus on your face before capturing.
More light helps the camera avoid motion blur.

presentation_maintain.title: Great shot setup
presentation_maintain.summary: Lighting, angle and framing look good. Use the same setup for future check-ins so you can compare fairly.
steps: Retake in the same spot and time of day to track progress.
